limitations: The direct network blocker is observed connection timeout; routing versus filtering versus other reachability causes was not identified.
Two already-observed interface pairs were tried with bounded deadlines. No broad scanning or firewall/DNS changes.
Only the first size/seed reached the direct-network stage before each bounded attempt failed. All 12 size/seed combinations completed host-local numerical generation separately.
Controller-aggregated candidate hashes are not evidence that both hosts independently adopted a shared candidate.
The fixed synthetic fixture does not establish Sybil resistance, privacy, poisoning resistance, WAN consensus, HCSN/LLM training or production deployment.
Data generator is stdlib random.gauss and source-pinned; this is a new controlled baseline, not the NumPy-generated parent from earlier PFT2.
Public evidence retains configured aliases, process and content hashes; private addresses, home paths and unrelated environment inventories are excluded.
multihost_recovery_status: NOT_REACHED: no direct incoming contribution triggered the planned exit/restart. Single-host transport recovery is separate evidence.

network_attempts.failure: TimeoutError: No direct incoming contribution before deadline
TimeoutError: No direct incoming contribution before deadline

timing_scope: Host elapsed_seconds measures local data generation/statistics/local solve only. It excludes tool launch, compression, operator retrieval and final controller validation; it is not end-to-end training latency.
transport_statement: Each configured host actually generated its own non-IID samples and computed its own G,b. Both direct TCP paths timed out without application bytes. The successful numerical result was collected and aggregated by the operator/controller, not exchanged peer to peer.
